cards.text: This psalm opens with one big word: "Hallelujah!" Then the writer turns and talks to himself: "Praise the LORD, O my soul." Friend, that's a man giving his own soul a pep talk, and I RESPECT it, because some mornings my soul needs one before the first oven's even warm.

cards.question: Right away, the writer makes a promise about praising the LORD. How long does he say he'll keep it up?

cards.text: Then the psalm slams on the brakes. Praise is on hold for one second, because here comes a warning: don't put your trust in princes.

cards.question: In this warning, the psalm calls princes mortal men who cannot save. True or false?

cards.text: And here's what mortal looks like. When a man's spirit departs, he returns to the ground, crown and all.

cards.question: The psalm says that when a prince dies, his plans live on after him. True or false?

cards.text: The five-year plan, the big strategy, the corner office? GONE, that very same day. Then the psalm flips it around: there IS a help worth having.

cards.question: The psalm says blessed is the one whose help comes from whom?

cards.text: Jacob is Israel's forefather, the man God renamed Israel (Gen 35:10), and his God is the One who MADE the ground the prince goes back to. The psalm calls Him "the Maker of heaven and earth, the sea, and everything in them."

cards.question: The psalm says the LORD stays faithful only as long as His people stay faithful. True or false?

cards.text: Now the psalm rolls out what this God actually does. Friend, the expired coupon I shared a junk drawer with never stopped believing in itself, and even IT would read this résumé and go quiet.

cards.question: First on the LORD's list: what does He do for the oppressed?
The list keeps going. The LORD gives food to the ___ and sets the ___ free.

cards.text: The LORD opens the eyes of the blind and lifts those who are weighed down. I spent years under a stack of old takeout menus, so that second one? PERSONAL.

cards.question: In the same verse, the psalm names who the LORD loves. Who is it?

cards.text: The LORD protects foreigners, and He sustains the fatherless and the widow. Then the psalm turns to one more group: the wicked.

cards.question: What does the LORD do to the ways of the wicked?
The psalm ends with a big claim about the God of Zion. The LORD reigns ___.

cards.text: And the psalm signs off right where it started: "Hallelujah!" Same word at the front door and the back door, friend, so praise gets the first word AND the last word.

findings.problem: Jacob first appears as a bare name in the correct answer. The baker is not told who he is until card 9, so his first appearance does not simply identify him.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The answers mix different kinds of things: "forever" and "for a season" describe the duration of the LORD's reign, while "from afar" describes its location or manner.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.

findings.problem: The card uses both verse 1, where the psalm opens with "Hallelujah!", and verse 10, where it closes with the same word, but it cites only Psalm 146:10.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
